title: Builder Signals · 2026-07-03
summary: Follow Builders 今日捕捉到 35 条 X 动态、1 集播客、0 篇博客；本站精选 10 条高信号内容。

featured.title: Aaron Levie · Box CEO
featured.summaryEn: Box CEO Aaron Levie latched onto Devin's "agentic mapreduce" concept to answer why the future needs 100X more AI inference. His take: we'll see swarms of agents processing massive data (like entire codebases) to do work humans never could — Devin maps relevant signals across a repo, fans out focused agents over bounded shards, reduces findings into one report, then verifies serious vulnerabilities in isolated sandboxes before confirming. Levie says this goes far beyond code security; Box customers already process…
featured.insightZh: Box CEO Aaron Levie 抓住 Devin 提出的「agentic mapreduce」概念，给出了一个关于未来为什么需要 100 倍 AI 推理算力的具体答案。他的判断是：接下来会出现成群的 agent 并行处理海量数据（比如整个代码库），完成人类过去根本无法企及的任务——Devin 的做法是先在仓库里 map 出相关信号，再 fan out 一批聚焦的子 agent 处理有界的分片，reduce 成一份报告，最后在隔离沙箱里验证严重漏洞才标记为确认。Levie 说这套模式远不止代码安全，Box 的客户已经在用它处理数百万份文档做风险、洞察、关系分析，未来会在制药、银行等一切非结构化数据的行业铺开。他还点出一个关键前提：这类能力通常只有在你能同时部署多种模型（前沿的 + 低成本的）时才可行，因为 token 消耗量太大——这将是应用层 AI 的核心价值主张。

featured.title: Matt Turck · FirstMark Capital VC、MAD Podcast 主持人
featured.summaryEn: FirstMark Capital's Matt Turck offered a sharp breakdown of Lime's successful IPO, fascinated by how a scooter company with $1B in debt — one that literally expressed "substantial doubt" about surviving the year — pulled it off in an AI-obsessed era. His points: impressive financial engineering (the IPO paid off toxic loans and converted the rest to equity for a clean slate); Uber owns 22% and refers riders directly, a great backstop; Lime has been FCF-positive for three straight years with revenue up nearly 30% Y…
featured.insightZh: FirstMark Capital 投资人 Matt Turck 对 Lime（共享滑板车公司）成功 IPO 做了一番精彩拆解，反差点在于：一家背着 10 亿美元债务、财报里刚写完「对能否活过今年存在重大疑虑」的公司，是怎么在 AI 独占眼球的时代逆势上市的。他归纳了几点：漂亮的财务工程（IPO 募资还清了有毒贷款、其余转成股权，一张干净的资产负债表）；Uber 持股 22% 并直接把用户导流给 Lime，是极好的后盾和合作方；公司实际上已连续三年自由现金流为正、营收同比增长近 30%；再加上「熬成微出行血战最后幸存者」（RIP Bird）的稀缺叙事。他还顺手吐槽：2026 年了，当下最火的 IPO 品牌居然是 AOL、Evernote、Vimeo 和 Lime。

featured.title: The AI Workflows Behind Every's Consulting Team
featured.summaryEn: AI is exceptional at executing against a standard operating procedure, but it needs two things — constant oversight/management, and a human to surface "what's interesting in the data." The real leverage is to stop doing individual emails and instead build the system (the loop) that does your emails for you. Guest Natalia is Every's head of consulting and manager of "Claudie," the firm's internal AI-employee agent. Her frontline view: Claudie has gone from novelty to an agent that works every day — it has its own LinkedIn and Twitter, manages dashboards, and runs a self-evaluation loop. But she's candid about the limits: AI is great at SOPs yet still needs constant oversight; taste and reaching for excellence require human direction; and rich dashboards still need a person to surface the signals. A counterintuitive call: despite being able to vibe-code a CRM, she chose to buy Atio + Asan…
featured.insightZh: AI 极擅长照着标准作业流程（SOP）执行，但它需要两样东西——持续的监督管理，以及人来从数据里挖出「什么才是有意思的信号」；真正的杠杆在于别再一封封写邮件，而是搭建替你做邮件的「系统/loop」。 嘉宾 Natalia 是 Every 的咨询业务负责人，也是内部 AI 员工 agent「Claudie」的管理者。她带来了一线视角：Claudie 如今已从「新奇玩具」变成每天干活的 agent，有自己的 LinkedIn 和 Twitter、管理仪表盘、还跑一个自我评估的循环来改进自己。但她坦言 AI 有明确边界——擅长照 SOP 执行，却仍需要持续监督，「品味」和追求卓越依然要靠人来指方向；而且再丰富的仪表盘也需要人来指出「数据里什么才是有意思的、信号是什么」。 一个反直觉的决定：明明团队有能力 vibe code 出一套 CRM，她却选择去买现成的 Atio + Asana。原因是「AI 时代你能造任何东西，真正的问题是你该不该去造并长期维护它」——数据质量的维护是别人的整门生意，把它外包出去反而释放了团队。她还大力安利 Codex，说它「让我不用再操心文件系统和文件夹结构，就是能用」，对非技术背景的人是 life-changing。她跑过最得意的一个 loop：给 Codex 一个目标——按邮件和通话记录把上百个客户对话准确填进 CRM，睡前启动，六小时后醒来 CRM 已经建好，完成了本来要花数周的活。 主持人 Dan Shipper 用了个精准的比喻收尾：知识工作正从「雕塑」（每一刀都靠你的手）变成「园艺」（你创造让生长发生的条件，但不是用手把植物捏出来）。这就是 loop 的本质——你不再做每一封邮件，而是搭建替你做邮件的系统，在关键处（开头和结尾的「人类三明治」）介入，并把每次学到的东西复利回系统。

items.title: Zara Zhang · Follow Builders 作者、独立 builder
items.summaryEn: Independent builder Zara Zhang shared a counterintuitive philosophy on building skills: you don't START with a skill, you END with one. Building the skill is the last step of your workflow, not the first — get the thing actually done and working first, iterate until it's smooth, then codify that proven process into a skill. She also dropped two practical notes: you can swap Codex's model to GLM (with instructions), and her full skill-building walkthrough is up on YouTube. The "do it first, codify later" ordering i…
items.insightZh: 独立 builder Zara Zhang 抛出了一个反直觉的 skill 构建心法：你不是从 skill 开始，而是以 skill 结束。构建 skill 是你工作流的最后一步，不是第一步——先把事情真正做出来、跑通、迭代顺，最后再把这套已验证的流程沉淀成 skill。她还分享了两个实用点：可以把 Codex 的模型换成 GLM（附操作），以及她的完整 skill 构建视频已上传 YouTube。这个「先做再沉淀」的顺序，对很多一上来就想搭框架的人是个很好的纠偏。

items.title: Guillermo Rauch · Vercel CEO
items.summaryEn: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch showed off running legacy WordPress on a modern serverless stack: WordPress on Vercel Fluid (Active CPU billing) from a single `Dockerfile.vercel`, MySQL on PlanetScale, 30-second deployments including cloud `docker build`, all via one command — `vercel`. He also announced a capability aimed squarely at agentic deployments: a dry-run step. Agents love to check their work before pushing (you see `tsc --noEmit`, `next build` etc. all over agent sessions), so Vercel now ships a dry-run for…
items.insightZh: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 秀了一把让老派 WordPress 跑在现代 serverless 栈上的操作：用单个 `Dockerfile.vercel` 把 WordPress 部署到 Vercel Fluid（Active CPU 计费），MySQL 托管在 PlanetScale，包含云端 `docker build` 在内 30 秒完成部署，一条命令 `vercel` 搞定。他同时宣布了对 agentic 部署很关键的新能力——dry-run 步骤：agent 在 push 前总爱先自查（你会在 agent session 里到处看到 `tsc --noEmit`、`next build` 之类），Vercel 现在为 agent 化部署提供 dry-run，把成本和风险降到最低。

items.title: Nikunj Kothari · FPV Ventures 合伙人
items.summaryEn: FPV Ventures partner Nikunj Kothari described the intensifying "talent vortex" pulling people into OpenAI and Anthropic — in the last two months, four personal friends left very established roles to join the labs. His read on the dual draw: building one of the most consequential companies plus the pre-IPO liquidity is just too hard to pass up. The implication: going out on your own now requires massive conviction and ambition. He added a sober note that most VCs actually won't make life-changing money — some have…
items.insightZh: FPV Ventures 合伙人 Nikunj Kothari 描述了 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 正在制造的「人才漩涡」——过去两个月，他有四个私交好友放弃了非常稳固的成熟岗位加入这两家 lab。他分析双重吸引力：既是在建一家最具历史意义的公司，又是 pre-IPO 阶段能拿到流动性，这诱惑实在太难抗拒。言下之意，如果你选择自己单干创业，就得有极强的信念和巨大的野心。他还补了一句现实：大多数 VC 其实赚不到多少钱、至少赚不到改变人生的钱——有些人正因为看清了这点才转投 lab。

items.title: Amjad Masad · Replit CEO
items.summaryEn: Replit CEO Amjad Masad flagged a shift in focus: now that building is easy, they're increasingly focused on getting entrepreneurs to market — reaching their first customer and first dollar. To that end he announced a Whop integration (which he calls one of the best places on the internet to monetize creations): you can now sell your Replit apps directly on Whop. It's a pragmatic signal of attention moving from "can you build it" to "can you sell it."
items.insightZh: Replit CEO Amjad Masad 点出团队重心的转移：既然「构建」这件事已经变得容易，他们越来越聚焦于帮创业者走向市场、触达第一个客户和赚到第一块钱。为此他宣布 Replit 打通了 Whop——他称之为互联网上变现创作的最佳场所之一——现在你可以直接在 Whop 上卖你用 Replit 做的 app。这是「能做出来」之后，把注意力转向「怎么卖出去」的一个务实信号。

items.title: Peter Yang · AI 教程与访谈创作者
items.summaryEn: AI tutorials creator Peter Yang gave the just-returned Claude Fable 5 a vibe check: still really good, a step function above any other model, and he hopes GPT 5.6 can match it. He made a new tutorial walking through five use cases worth trying Fable on — finding Fable-worthy work, getting life and business advice, making projects ship-ready, planning the next big thing, and refactoring your project or codebase — all no-BS with Fable's actual output shown. As someone still learning to read code, he's also eager to…
items.insightZh: AI 教程创作者 Peter Yang 给刚回归的 Claude Fable 5 下了「氛围体检」结论：依然强得离谱，比其他任何模型都高出一个台阶，他希望 GPT 5.6 能追上。他为此做了新教程，走了 5 个值得用 Fable 试的场景：找到值得 Fable 出手的工作、获取人生与商业建议、把项目打磨到可发布、规划下一件大事、重构你的项目或代码库——全程无废话，直接展示 Fable 的真实输出。作为一个仍在学读代码的人，他还兴奋地要装 explain-diff skill。注意窗口期：Fable 5 只到 7 月 7 日可在 Claude 订阅里用。

items.title: Claude (Anthropic) · 官方账号
items.summaryEn: Anthropic's official Claude account shared the details on Fable 5's return: all paid plans with usage included can access Fable 5 through July 7, up to 50% of your weekly usage limit, after which you can switch models or keep using Fable via usage credits. It also noted Claude Code's false-positive handling — if a request is mistakenly flagged, run `/feedback` to file a report (thumbs buttons on web and Cowork), which helps tune the classifiers and reduce false positives over time.
items.insightZh: Anthropic 官方账号 Claude 宣布 Fable 5 回归的使用细节：所有含用量额度的付费方案都能在 7 月 7 日前访问 Fable 5，可用量上限为每周额度的 50%，超出后可切换到其他模型，也可继续用 usage credits 使用 Fable。同时官方提到 Claude Code 的误报处理机制——如果你的请求被错误标记，可以用 `/feedback` 提交报告，网页版和 Cowork 上可通过点赞/点踩按钮反馈，这些反馈会用于持续调优分类器、减少误报。

items.title: Peter Steinberger · OpenClaw ClawFather
items.summaryEn: OpenClaw's Peter Steinberger gave Steve Yegge a shoutout he never thought he'd give: Yegge was just early, like most visionaries — now everyone is building factories. Behind the brief note is a clear trend in agentic coding: moving from single agents doing work to building factory-style agent systems that produce at scale. He's also hunting for a semi-private hack space in SF for a few days to cook with some OpenClaw maintainers.
items.insightZh: OpenClaw 的 Peter Steinberger 给了 Steve Yegge 一个他自己都没想到会给的致敬：Yegge 只是早了一步，像大多数有远见的人一样——如今人人都在造「工厂」（factories）。这条简短感言背后是当下 agentic coding 的一个明显趋势：从单个 agent 干活，转向搭建能规模化产出的 agent 工厂式系统。他这几天还在 SF 找一个半私密的 hack space，要和几位 OpenClaw 维护者闭关「开火做饭」。
